title: Dub 241 Dotted
notes: THE DOTTED-EIGHTH ECHO, the delay both Signs of Life sources treat as the genre's default. Round two used 3/16 on three pieces, but each under a full stab figure; here the delay is the figure. 125 BPM, F minor, and the stab plays only TWICE a bar - on the 'and' of one and of three - because at 3/16 each stab answers itself three steps later and again three after that, and the echoes fill every gap the stab left. The least notes of any piece in the round, and the most rhythm.

title: Dub 243 Nest
notes: FOUR LOOP LENGTHS AT ONCE. 125 BPM, Bb dorian. The kick loops every bar, the bass every HALF bar (1/32, sixteen steps in two beats), the stab every two bars (1/8) and the pad every four (1/4) - so the figure never lands the same way twice inside a phrase, which is what polymeter is for, reached with the divisions this instrument has. Not true 5-against-4: a pattern's length here is a whole number of bars or a half bar, and the round says so rather than pretending.
